appearance_facts.fact: The chart title is 'Monthly Grid Energy Use (kWh)' in bold black text.
The vertical axis is labeled 'Grid energy use (kWh)' with tick marks at 10,000, 15,000, 20,000, 25,000, 30,000, and 40,000.
The horizontal axis is labeled 'Month' with tick marks for 'Apr', 'Jan', 'Jun', 'Feb', 'Mar', and 'May'.
The bar for 'May' is the shortest bar on the chart, visually below the 10,000 kWh mark.
The bar for 'Jan' is the tallest bar, reaching the 40,000 kWh mark.
The bar for 'Apr' is the second tallest, reaching the 30,000 kWh mark.
The bars for 'Mar', 'Feb', and 'Jun' are all approximately the same height, around the 20,000 to 25,000 kWh range.
All bars are solid dark red.

printed_facts.fact: Data point for May is visually below the 10,000 kWh mark.
Data point for Jan is at 40,000 kWh.
Data point for Apr is at 30,000 kWh.
Data points for Mar, Feb, and Jun are approximately at 20,000-25,000 kWh.

public_definitions: The task is to review the monthly grid energy dashboard to decide if May's low-usage should be routed as a standard case or escalated as a critical anomaly.
The decision is based solely on the visual data presented in the bar chart.
The chart displays energy usage in kWh for various months, with May being the month of interest.
The three routing options are: standard follow-up, critical anomaly review, or background filing.
uncertain: The exact kWh value for May is not labeled, only its relative position below 10,000 kWh.
